metadata.updatePolicy: What’s New is curated for the people who use Ozzie. User-facing features, support-content changes, and visible bug fixes are shown to everyone. Admin-only operational or administrative changes are shown only to administrators. Developer-only work such as refactors, tests, commits, backups, and deployment mechanics is not listed unless it changes how Ozzie is used or operated.

updates.title: New Call now starts a clean support session
updates.changed: Added a New Call action that clears the current device, caller role, active troubleshooting path, search, and unsaved Call Documentation draft only after an in-app confirmation. Saved notes, favorites, training progress, and workspace settings are not deleted.

Choose New Call and Cancel; confirm the current context and unsaved draft remain unchanged.
Choose New Call → Start New Call and confirm the Home troubleshooting state returns to a clean session.
Confirm the unsaved Call Documentation draft is cleared while previously saved notes remain available.

updates.title: Common Issues now helps you find the right approved guide
updates.changed: Common Issues now focuses on the caller’s symptom and device, recommends the matching approved Process Guide, surfaces the official Zoom Support article that best matches the selected device or meeting state, and includes a concise “Why this route?” explanation. The explanation shows the actual decision factor—such as device or exact screen state—and clearly distinguishes retained call context like caller role from information that changed the recommendation.
checks: Open I can’t hear anyone, select Android and a caller role, then expand Why this route?; confirm Android is identified as the device-specific routing factor and the role is described only as retained context.
Switch between Windows and Android and confirm the recommendation, highlighted Zoom source, and route explanation stay aligned.
Open I’m waiting to get in, choose Waiting Room, and confirm Why this route? identifies the exact Waiting Room screen state as the routing reason.
Confirm coverage-gap paths still stop without inventing a recommendation or route explanation.

updates.title: Process Guides now give device-specific troubleshooting one step at a time
updates.changed: Call Guides now preserve device-specific approved steps, matched Zoom sources, symptom-aware end-of-path routing, optional documentation handoff, and live call context across chained troubleshooting. If the agent changes the device inside a Guided Process, that device follows into the next approved Common Issue together with the caller role, so the next route does not ask for the same context again.
checks: Start Bluetooth troubleshooting from Android with a caller role selected, then change the device to Windows inside the Guided Process.

Confirm changing the device inside a Process Guide also updates the active device captured in workspace/report context.
Confirm normal Common Issue → Guided Process handoffs still preserve the selected device and role.
Confirm Call Documentation handoffs still append only the troubleshooting actually completed and do not auto-save.

updates.title: Final pilot usability pass hardens the workspace across screen sizes
updates.changed: Completed a final pre-pilot usability pass focused on keeping authenticated workspace pages readable and reachable across desktop, short browser windows, tablets, and mobile screens. Added shared overflow and reflow protection for page content and controls, protected long navigation menus in short windows, improved the Process Documents reader under the mobile header, and expanded Feedback Queue Open Page routing so reports from Favorites, Process Documents, Saved Notes, Admin, and other workspace pages return to the correct page instead of defaulting to Home.

updates.title: Original Process Documents now have their own Knowledge library
updates.changed: Added a dedicated Process Documents page under Knowledge so agents can browse the original source documents directly by process title instead of opening a Process Guide first. The library is searchable, shows the source-page count for each process, and opens a full-page reader with the original rendered pages, page numbering, and an Open full size option. Existing Process Guides, Common Issues, and their source references remain unchanged.

updates.changed: Improved the shared Process Guide drawer so Call Guide, Visual Guide, Source Pages, and Full Process remain available at the top while the content below scrolls. updates.changed: Added My Saved Notes for regular users so saved call notes and follow-ups can be reviewed outside the documentation dock. updates.changed: Expanded the Admin Saved Notes workspace with a dedicated follow-up view, filtering and person-level drill-down so protected notes can be reviewed more efficiently. updates.title: Phase 8 stabilization closes with final smoke and freeze
updates.changed: Completed the final stabilization gate across Member, Lead, and Admin workspace surfaces. Added a dedicated responsive smoke test covering desktop, tablet/mobile navigation behavior, role-specific navigation, Back-button availability, and the production shell breakpoints. Production data sanity checks found no missing workspace roles, invalid claimed/pending slots, or orphaned Favorites/Recently Viewed rows. This closes Phase 8; future feature ideas should begin in a new phase rather than being folded into stabilization.

updates.title: Data boundaries hardened after role and personalization updates
updates.changed: Completed the post-enhancement data and permission regression. Normal accounts can now directly update only their avatar and Ozzie onboarding state; sensitive profile fields such as Admin role, account status, workspace role, and username are no longer writable through self-service table access. Recently Viewed now runs under the signed-in user’s RLS permissions and is unavailable anonymously. Live rollback-only probes confirmed Member and Lead accounts remain non-admin, Favorites/Recently Viewed stay owner-scoped, Readiness admin reporting remains Admin-only, Ozzie marking is idempotent, and permanent-delete relationships still cascade to user-owned workspace data.

updates.changed: Completed the component and copy-hygiene pass. Shared data and formatting helpers were separated from React component files so Fast Refresh no longer raises structural warnings. updates.title: Readiness Lab Part 5 completes live-call readiness validation
updates.changed: Completed the five-part Readiness Lab with Part 5, a separate five-question persistent validation set that combines call flow, discovery, troubleshooting discipline, resolution confirmation, scope/referral judgment, and evidence-based documentation. The scenarios test listening and identifying context before technical action, stopping and reassessing when the caller’s screen differs, properly confirming and closing a resolved call, handling an unresolved managed-permission boundary without promising a direct Zoom escalation, and documenting only the issue, steps, results, next step/contact, and outcome that actually occurred. Part 5 keeps its own up-to-three-attempt history, uses discovery-based Training & Resources lookup, and appears as a separate JA Usage Analytics report section. The Training Roadmap now marks all five Readiness Lab parts available.

updates.title: Readiness Lab Part 4 adds scope and referral judgment
updates.changed: Added Readiness Lab Part 4 as a separate five-question persistent validation set focused on deciding whether support should continue, stop, or hand off to the correct owner. The questions cover continuing approved basic troubleshooting when the next step stays in scope, Waiting Room admission owned by the host or organizer, account/license/admin access owned by organization IT or the Zoom administrator, hardware not detected by the device owned by IT/device support, and privacy/recording/proceeding-policy decisions owned by the meeting organizer or designated arbitration/client contact. Part 4 keeps its own up-to-three-attempt history, retains discovery-based Training & Resources lookup, and is reported separately in JA Usage Analytics. Part 5 remains locked.

updates.title: Readiness Lab Part 3 adds troubleshooting judgment
updates.changed: Added Readiness Lab Part 3 as a separate five-question persistent validation set focused on what the agent should do after a troubleshooting result changes the situation. The questions cover a failed-join call that becomes a Waiting Room state, joining meeting audio before deeper output checks, recognizing when the operating system itself cannot see a microphone, stopping deeper camera recovery once the expected preview returns, and moving to the device/browser capture-permission path when screen sharing reaches that layer. Part 3 keeps its own up-to-three-attempt history, uses the discovery-based Training & Resources lookup, and is reported separately in JA Usage Analytics. Parts 4–5 remain locked.

updates.title: Live Call Flow aligned to the new Ogletree Tier 1 standard
updates.changed: Replaced the older seven-stage call journey with the current Ogletree Tier 1 Zoom Support flow: Opening / Greeting → Active Listening & Acknowledgment → Empathy Statement → Assurance / Ownership → Caller & Hearing Identification → Probing / Diagnostic Questions → Troubleshooting → Confirmation of Resolution → Recap / Summary → Final Check → Closing. Navigator now captures Hearing Status and who is affected early in the call, shows the source’s simple Greet → Listen → Empathize → Assure → Probe → Troubleshoot → Confirm → Close formula, and displays the resolved versus unresolved branch after confirmation. Locate → Describe → Guide → Confirm remains the troubleshooting method inside Step 7 rather than the entire call flow. Training Roadmap, Call Language, Guided Visual Lessons, and Scenario Scripts were aligned to the new sequence.

updates.title: Scope Check now completes the referral handoff
updates.changed: Extended Scope Check with the approved referral / roadblock matrix. When a case reaches Stop + Refer, agents now choose the exact roadblock and the workspace identifies who owns the next step, shows the agent boundary, provides source-backed handoff wording, and lets the agent copy that wording. The tool covers Waiting Room admission, host-controlled permissions, incorrect meeting details, unresolved joining issues, account/admin access, device-level hardware detection, organization-managed permissions, network/security restrictions, possible Zoom product issues after basic troubleshooting, proceeding decisions, and privacy/recording/confidentiality/AI-policy questions. The workspace does not invent a person, phone number, email address, or promise an internal escalation.

updates.title: Scope Check now tells agents when to continue or stop
updates.changed: Added a global Scope Check live tool beside Call Documentation. Agents can classify the remaining action, indicate how far approved troubleshooting has progressed, and confirm whether the next step stays within approved authority. The workspace then returns Continue Approved Troubleshooting, Stop + Refer, Resolved — Document & Close, or More Information Needed. The decision path follows the approved Zoom Basic Support Boundaries resource and does not invent referral contacts or promise internal escalation. The Navigator resolution status was also renamed from Escalation Needed to Referral Needed to match the approved handoff model.

updates.title: Call Documentation moved to a global docked live tool
updates.changed: Moved Call Documentation out of Training & Resources and into the authenticated sidebar as a global live tool. Opening Call Documentation no longer navigates away from the agent’s current page. updates.title: Common Issue Routes added to Navigator
updates.changed: Added the first Phase 2 live-call routing layer for five high-frequency concerns: Can’t join the meeting, I can’t hear anyone, They can’t hear me, My camera isn’t working, and I’m waiting to get in. Each route starts from the caller’s symptom, asks only the questions that change the path, separates symptoms from assumed causes, shows one-step-at-a-time guidance and expected results, keeps Waiting for host distinct from Waiting Room, carries forward the Phase 1 device/role/status context, and preserves access to approved Process Documents plus traceable official Zoom Support sources. Natural caller-language search now surfaces these fast routes before deeper process results when appropriate.

Supabase hardening also removed unintended client execution of an internal SECURITY DEFINER helper, moved citext out of the exposed public schema, optimized RLS auth checks, and added missing foreign-key indexes.
